VII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|307}}</noinclude>fathers first: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=13}}† and at the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 45.''}}* second time Ioseph vvas knovven of his brethren, and his kinred vvas made knovven vnto Pharao. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=14}}† And Ioseph sending, called thither Iacob his father and al his kinred in seuentie fiue soules. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=15}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 46.''}}* Iacob descended into Ægypt: and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 49. Gen. 50.''}}* he died, and our fathers. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=16}}† And they vvere {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 23.''}}* translated into Sichem, and vvere {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ios. 24.''}}* laid in the sepulchre that Abraham {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Translation of Saincts bodies agreable to nature & Scripture. And the desire to be buried in one place more then an other (vvhich the holy Patriarches also had ''Gen. 49, 29. 50, 24. Hebr. 11, 22'') hath sometime great causes. ''Aug. de Cur. pro mort. c. 1. & vlt''.}}∷ bought for a price of siluer of the sonnes of Hemor the sonne of Sichem.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=17}}† And vvhen the time drevv neere of the promisse vvhich God had promised to Abraham, the people {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 1, 7.''}}* increased and vvas multiplied in Ægypt, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=18}}† vntil an other king arose in Ægypt, that knevv not Ioseph. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=19}}† This same circumuenting our stocke, afflicted our fathers: that they should expose their children, to the end they might not be kept aliue. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=20}}† The same time vvas {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 2, 2.''}}* Moyses borne, and he vvas acceptable to God, who was nourished three moneths in his fathers house. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=21}}† And vvhen he vvas exposed, Pharaos daughter tooke him vp, and nourished him for her ovvne sonne. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=22}}† And Moyses vvas instructed in al the vvisedom of the Ægyptians: and he vvas mightie in his vvordes and vvorkes. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=23}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 2, 11.''}}* vvhen he vvas fully of the age of fourtie yeres, it came to his minde to visite his brethren the children of Israël. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=24}}† And vvhen he had seen one suffer vvrong, he defended him: and striking the Ægyptian, he reuenged his quarel that susteined the vvrong. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=25}}† And he thought that his brethren did vnderstand that God by his hand vvould saue them: but they vnderstoode it not. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=26}}† And the day folovving {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 2, 13.''}}* he appeared to them being at strife: and he reconciled them vnto peace, saying, Men, ye are brethren, vvherfore hurt you one an other? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=27}}† But he that did the iniurie to his neighbour, repelled him, saying, ''Vvho hath appointed thee prince and iudge ouer vs''? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=28}}† ''Vvhat, vvilt thou kil me, as thou didst yesterday kil the Ægyptian''? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=29}}† And Moyses fled vpon this vvord: and he became a soiourner in the land of Mádian, vvhere he begat tvvo sonnes. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=30}}† And after fourtie yeres vvere expired, there {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 3, 2.''}}* appeared to him in the desert of mount Sina an Angel in the fire of the flame of a bush. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=31}}† And Moyses seeing it, marueled at the vision. And as he vvent neere to vevve it, the voice of our Lord vvas made to him, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=32}}† ''I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob''. And Moyses being made to tremble, durst not vevve it. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=33}}† And our Lord<noinclude>{{rh||Qq ij|said}}</noinclude>
